notes: The player save command writes the pfile and a RENT_CRASH crash file; after <RESTART> the re-entry inventory restores the carried loaf and score restores the pfile fields, proving both halves of the round trip.
The boot prune keeps the fresh RENT_CRASH file (the 10-day timeout is far away), so the explicitly saved state survives the bounce.
<CRASH> kills both engines with no graceful saves; the restore comes purely from the earlier explicit save, identical bytes to the graceful path.
No save and no autosave window (600 pulses, none pumped): a crash with an unsaved carried object loses it on both engines — the re-entry inventory is empty. C's per-boot state, not a port bug (R4).

store_to_char full-heals only at >= 1 real hour away; a restart relogin is seconds, so the drained hit points (5 of 500 via set player) survive the bounce in the compared score. The >= 1 hour heal arm stays unit-level (R5f): no oracle scenario can wait an hour.

quit outside a save room answers the REALLYQUIT warning, REALLYQUIT departs with "$n has left the game.", and the deferred extraction (one pumped pulse) drops the carried loaf to the floor where the observing peer's look finds it.
